applies_why: Yes, the judge text grounds STANDS on a challenger witness or witnesses not stating the link.
quote: D3: STANDS -- [CR2] D answers the “born of a woman” idiom and Hebrews 10:5; C5 shows the body is fitted for the offering but does not state that a man begat the child. GROUND: no challenger witness names a human father for this conception.
rule_words: That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side.
room: a single verse does not state a link or its contrary — I weighed reading it narrowly as only an isolated verse's non-statement, versus reading it as barring non-statement of the link by a verse or set of cited verses.
why: The judge's D3 STANDS ruling rests on 'no challenger witness names a human father,' which is using a verse or witnesses not stating the link as a ground forbidden by K-S2.
